program_title: Beyond Live Sound Engineering Internship — 180-Day Program
purpose: Prepare interns to perform live sound engineering work safely, ethically, measurably, reproducibly, and professionally under Beyond supervision.
global_rules: Protect hearing, inspect cables and rigging, calculate electrical load, use safe lifting, and keep outputs muted or gains minimum during connection changes. Never expose people or equipment to unsafe levels.
Work only inside authorized boundaries and on assigned assets.
Capture evidence during work; preserve prior evidence and restore the approved state.
Use official/vendor sources, approved tools, rated hardware, valid licences, and qualified supervision.
Protect secrets, personal/client data, recordings, equipment details, and production information.
Document measurements, uncertainty, errors, troubleshooting, time, assistance, incidents, and limitations honestly.

phases.name: Live Sound Capstone and Professional Readiness

days.topic: Safety, Hearing Protection, and Workflow
days.objective: Complete a supervised hearing, electrical, cable, lifting, gain-at-minimum, and emergency mute readiness check before producing amplified sound.
learning_outcomes: Explain Safety, Hearing Protection, and Workflow in clear professional language.
Use Beyond mixers, microphones, PPE to complete the objective inside the approved boundary.

Produce measurable, independently verified evidence for: Complete a supervised hearing, electrical, cable, lifting, gain-at-minimum, and emergency mute readiness check before producing amplified sound.
Apply Beyond safety, ethics, quality, documentation, rollback, and human-approval standards.
practical_procedure: Review the Day 1 scope, prerequisite from Day 0, and supervisor instructions before touching software, accounts, cables, power, rigging, networks, or equipment.
Confirm the authorized lab/equipment boundary, owner, asset IDs, workspace condition, backup/rollback state, emergency procedure, and any PPE or spotter requirement.

Verify only the approved tools for today: Beyond mixers, microphones, PPE, Beyond audio system, SPL meter, checklists. Record versions, firmware, serial/asset references, calibration status, or configuration as relevant. Avoid unnecessary installation or updates.
Create Day_001_safety_hearing_protection_and_workflow with evidence, diagrams or src, checklists or tests, output, and report folders.
Capture a privacy-reviewed baseline photograph/screenshot and record expected result, measurement units, acceptance limit, and stop condition.
Complete the practical objective: Complete a supervised hearing, electrical, cable, lifting, gain-at-minimum, and emergency mute readiness check before producing amplified sound.
Introduce or analyze only an approved controlled fault/edge case. Troubleshoot systematically, preserve evidence, and return the lab/equipment to its approved state.
Verify independently through a second instrument/path/test, clean rerun, configuration comparison, peer check, or supervisor sign-off. Distinguish evidence from proof.
Complete the discipline safety/ethics checklist, inventory/custody or cleanup check, and a professional report with honest limitations and assistance disclosure.
safety_ethics_and_beyond_lab_rules: Protect hearing, inspect cables and rigging, calculate electrical load, use safe lifting, and keep outputs muted or gains minimum during connection changes. Never expose people or equipment to unsafe levels.
Use only assigned labs, equipment, data, accounts, frequencies, networks, repositories, venues, and test targets. Stop if authorization or ownership is unclear.

Do not expose secrets, private/client data, personal communications, production identifiers, unsafe images, or unrelated backgrounds in code, prompts, repositories, recordings, photographs, screenshots, or reports.

Never bypass guards, interlocks, PPE, access controls, rated loads, electrical protection, change approval, licences, or vendor limits. Do not improvise unsafe adapters, rigging, mains power, scans, exploits, or public exposure.

Use approved rollback, mute/power-down, backup, snapshot, restore, isolation, or safe-strike procedures before and after changes. Report accidental exposure, injury risk, damage, data loss, or boundary crossing immediately.

Disclose AI/tool assistance and verify every generated instruction, calculation, configuration, claim, measurement, and recommendation. Record time, errors, troubleshooting, incidents, limitations, and equipment condition honestly.
self_check_questions: Can you explain Safety, Hearing Protection, and Workflow to a supervisor in under two minutes without reading?

What evidence proves that you completed “Complete a supervised hearing, electrical, cable, lifting, gain-at-minimum, and emergency mute readiness check before producing amplified sound.” rather than merely watching or copying a result?
Which safety, privacy, security, electrical, mechanical, hearing, data-quality, operational, or authorization failure is most relevant today?
What measurement or acceptance criterion did you use, and what are its limitations?
How did you independently verify the result and restore the approved state?
What would you check first if the demonstration failed five minutes before review?
Why is the result ready—or not ready—for real use, and who must approve the next action?

evidence_checklist.requirement: Privacy-reviewed baseline showing the authorized workspace, isolation/boundary, assigned tools or equipment, and safe starting state.
Configurations, code, diagrams, checklists, measurements, tests, and outputs needed to reproduce the work; exclude secrets and unauthorized data.
Expected versus observed result, acceptance criterion, and independent second test, measurement, peer review, or supervisor sign-off.
Completed safety/ethics check plus proof of rollback, cleanup, inventory/custody, safe power-down/strike, or restored lab state as applicable.
Professional report covering scope, concepts, tools/equipment, procedure, measurements, results, risks, verification, troubleshooting, limitations, restoration, assistance disclosure, and references.

days.required_submission: Baseline evidence, completed practical artifact, independent verification, safety/restoration record, and short professional report.
days.prerequisite: Program admission, assigned authorized workstation/equipment, and approved lab or venue boundary.
report_sections: Concepts in the student’s own words

Safety, ethics, security, privacy, quality, and human approval
